analysis:
Both units are head_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, in the historical sections (roughly v0.8.13 to v0.10.x). The visible patch hunk covers lines 11-176 only, and the supplied excerpts do not include those lines. Lines 2387-3014 are therefore pre-existing historical release notes, not new behavior. No code, configuration, protocol, key handling, authorization or attestation logic is changed in the supplied units. The changelog documents provider/coordinator behavior only as prose. Documentation-only changes do not alter the threat model's controls, so no regression is attributable to them.

The one security-relevant claim I could check is the SSD prefix-cache description in the historical notes, which is consistent with T-041. It describes encrypted, authenticated checkpoints bound to tenant, model, prompt, binary and metallib identity, with a global kill switch and cold fallback. The v0.9.1 note sizes the cache at half of available disk, with a 20 GiB write reserve, a 90% novel-write share and a 30-minute TTL. These match the documented T-041 posture, so no TTL or tenant-scoping change needs sign-off from these lines.

The candidate section at lines 11-176, which describes MLX pin updates, the sandbox installer/add-on interaction and the TB-012/TB-013 or T-061 surface, is not visible in these units. Any security conclusion about it, including how the claimed `darkbloom sandbox` installer is fetched, verified and run, is outside this evidence. Another pass should examine the actual code changes and the head lines for that range. The `needs_deeper_review` flag is set for that coverage gap, not for a suspected defect.
